items.a: It depends on team size, not the plan price alone. GoHighLevel's Starter plan and ClickFunnels' Launch plan both cost $97 a month, so the entry price is a tie. GoHighLevel charges that flat rate no matter how many users or contacts you add, then bills texts, calls, email and most AI separately from a prepaid wallet. ClickFunnels caps Launch at 2 team-member seats and 10,000 contacts, and needing more of either forces an upgrade to Scale at $197 or Optimize at $297 a month. For a small team of three people, GoHighLevel's own cost scenario runs $125.42 a month, driven mostly by messaging usage, while ClickFunnels needs the $197 Scale plan just to add a third staff seat. A solo operator with light messaging usually lands close to $97 a month on either one, with GoHighLevel's wallet adding a small amount for any texts or calls sent.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel replace ClickFunnels for building funnels?
items.a: GoHighLevel includes a funnel and website builder on every plan, starting at $97 a month for Starter, so it can replace ClickFunnels' core job of building a page and checkout flow for most sellers. What GoHighLevel adds beyond that is a full CRM, calendars and a phone and texting system, which ClickFunnels does not build in. What it does not match is ClickFunnels' course and community depth: ClickFunnels bundles 3 courses on its $97 Launch plan, rising to 20 on its top Dominate plan, as a core part of the product, while GoHighLevel treats courses as a smaller piece alongside its CRM. A seller who only wants a funnel and a following can likely move to GoHighLevel's builder without missing much; a course-first business will notice GoHighLevel's funnel and course tools are not its main focus, and may prefer to keep the two roles separate instead of consolidating into one platform.

items.q: Does ClickFunnels have a CRM like GoHighLevel?
items.a: ClickFunnels bundles a CRM into its platform alongside funnels, an online store, courses, community and email tools, so it is not a bare funnel builder. What ClickFunnels does not publish is how deep that CRM goes: its plans are scoped by workspace count, team-member seats and contact limits, such as 10,000 contacts on the $97 Launch plan and up to 400,000 on Dominate, rather than by CRM features. GoHighLevel, by contrast, is built around its CRM and sales pipelines first, with unlimited contacts and unlimited users on every plan, including the same $97 Starter tier, and adds a full phone and texting system on top. A business that wants pipeline stages and phone-based follow-up as the main event is better served by GoHighLevel's CRM-first design; a business that wants a CRM bundled alongside a funnel and course platform, rather than as the centerpiece, gets that from ClickFunnels.

items.q: Which one is better for a marketing agency with multiple clients?
items.a: GoHighLevel is the more direct fit for billing multiple clients through the platform itself. Its Unlimited plan ($297 a month) lets an agency rebill phone and email usage to clients at cost, and Agency Pro ($497 a month) adds a marked-up SaaS mode so a client's subscription fee can flow through GoHighLevel's own billing instead of a separate invoice. ClickFunnels has no matching feature: its workspaces run from 1 on Launch to 20 on Dominate and give each client a separate area to build in, but nothing in its plans or terms lets an agency charge a client through ClickFunnels itself, so that billing has to happen outside the platform, through your own invoicing tool. An agency reselling access to a branded platform gets that specifically from GoHighLevel's Unlimited or Agency Pro plans; one that just needs separate workspaces per client, and invoices those clients on its own, can run that from either tool.

items.q: Do GoHighLevel or ClickFunnels take a percentage of sales?
items.a: Neither one takes a cut of what you sell. ClickFunnels' pricing-page FAQ states directly that it takes 0% of each sale on every plan, from the $97 Launch tier up to Dominate; you keep the full sale price minus whatever your card processor charges. Card payments on ClickFunnels run through Stripe or its own Payments AI gateway, both listed at the standard 2.9% rate plus a small flat fee per transaction, which is a processor charge, not a ClickFunnels fee. GoHighLevel does not publish a percent-of-sales fee either; its plan price, starting at $97 a month for Starter, covers the CRM, funnel and website tools outright, and the costs that do vary are for texting, calling, email and AI usage rather than for a share of revenue. The real difference between the two is not a sales cut on either side, but how each one prices everything else it bundles around your checkout.

items.q: Which one should a course creator choose?
items.a: ClickFunnels is the closer fit for most course creators. Its plans bundle courses directly, from 3 courses on the $97 Launch plan up to 20 on Dominate, alongside the funnel, email and community tools a course launch actually uses, and it takes no percentage of the sales that come through those funnels. GoHighLevel also includes courses and communities, but they sit alongside a full CRM, calendars and a phone and texting system that a course creator typically will not touch, while its $97 Starter plan still requires setting up A2P texting registration before sending a single SMS reminder. The exception is a course creator who is also running an agency-style business with multiple client accounts or heavy calling and texting for enrollment follow-up; that workflow leans back toward GoHighLevel's CRM and sub-account structure. For a course creator focused on selling and delivering courses through funnels and email, ClickFunnels' course-first bundling is the more direct match.
